newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures finish higher in quiet session.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures finish higher in quiet session.

text.p: U.S. debt futures finished firm after a quiet session.
September Eurodollar futures posted a fresh three-week high during the day, and June Treasury bond futures closed higher on the week after seven weeks of lower weekly closes.
Still, June remained bound within Thursday's daily range.
Traders said debt futures held a mildly positive technical bias after gains on Thursday, but many players took to the sidelines on Friday amid a dearth of significant economic data.
University of Michigan consumer sentiment was the only report Friday and provoked scant reaction in futures.

Market sources said April preliminary University of Michigan consumer sentiment was 101.0 versus the 100 March final index. The expectations index was 90.9 compared with March's 93.6, and current conditions registered 116.7 compared with 109.8.
June T-bonds upticked to the day's high at 108-4/32 in the minutes after the data, but traders said it was more of a bullish technical tone that led the market.
June closed above 107-24/32 on Thursday, with that firm tone carrying over into the pre-weekend lull on Friday, traders said. Resistance at 108-7/32 and 108-8/32 held.
May T-bond and note options expired without a hitch at midday.
Traders said mild bullish followthrough could emerge early Monday, given that June T-bonds broke their string of seven lower weekly closes.

"This is the first higher weekly close we've had in a while," one trader said. "Technically the market looks like it's at least doing okay this week, but we're still in a bear market," the trader said.
He deemed action very light, calling trade "worse than quiet."

At the close, June T-bonds were 05/32 higher at 108-00, June 10-year notes were up 04/32 at 106-02/32, September Eurodollars were up 0.025 at 93.77, and September T-bills were up 0.025 at 94.35. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750)) E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
